clue.text: Herb a little woman found in the grass

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other piece in this clue

parts.note: marram is a coarse grass of sand dunes
Jo is one of the four March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a herb that some girl planted among the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little woman' is not a small lady but one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic culinary plant of the mint family, a common kitchen herb.

clue.text: Place of work the French set up that's used in art, especially

definitions.text: Place of work the French set up that's used in art, especially

parts.words: Place of work the French set up that's used in art, especially
parts.note: a workroom named with a word borrowed from French, the term used above all for a painter's or sculptor's studio

explanation.walkthrough: 'the French set up' looks like LE reversed, but no parse gives the letters; the clue describes a French-named workplace used chiefly by artists.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is a studio or workshop, especially one where an artist or designer works.

clue.text: Times going into project with a stance put together

indicators.note: going into says one piece enters the other in this clue

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a pose is a stance or posture

explanation.surface: A newspaper's staff join a scheme while striking a posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X; 'project' is the verb, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To juxtapose things is to place them side by side, set close together for comparison.

clue.text: Pick up a summary

definitions.meaning: to carry on again after a break
a written outline of a career or an abstract of a text

explanation.definitionFit: To start again after a pause, or (as résumé) a brief account of the main points.

clue.text: It may result in time being ten to two, say

definitions.text: It may result in time being ten to two, say

parts.words: It may result in time being ten to two, say
parts.note: a jury split ten to two can still convict, sending someone to prison to do time

explanation.definitionFit: A jury decision reached without unanimity, such as ten jurors against two, permitted in English courts.

clue.text: Almost provide complete contents for short book of pictures

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter here

parts.note: to fill something is to provide complete contents for it
Mic. is the short form of Micah, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone nearly finishes stuffing a little picture book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last L of FILL to leave FIL. 'short book of pictures' reads like a comic, but 'short' only shortens Micah, and 'of pictures' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Filmic is an adjective meaning relating to motion pictures, the cinema.

clue.text: Iron skirt and edges of negligee suitable for woman

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: edges of says take the first and last letters of the word negligee

explanation.surface: Pressing a skirt and the hem of a nightdress seems ladylike work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a verb about pressing clothes; it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminine means having qualities traditionally associated with women, appropriate to womanhood.

clue.text: Turned up stuff on whale in island

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word reads from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to jam is to stuff or cram
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: Some flotsam washes up on a whale near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts ORCA beneath MAJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca, Mallorca in Spanish, is the largest of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Sheep shelters found round South-West, over the hill here?

definitions.text: Sheep shelters found round South-West, over the hill here?

indicators.note: found round says the first piece goes around the following pieces here

parts.note: cots, or cotes, are small shelters for sheep
over the hill means past one's prime, so old

explanation.surface: A guidebook mentions sheep pens around England's south-west hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: hilly English sheep country, wealthy from wool, lying in the south-west of the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cotswolds are a range of limestone hills in south-west central England, historically famous for sheep and the wool trade.

clue.text: Former king suffering setback at Salamis, initially

definitions.text: Former king suffering setback at Salamis, initially

indicators.note: a setback turns things back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
rex is Latin for king, as in the R of royal cyphers

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word Salamis

explanation.surface: A history note on a Persian monarch defeated in the sea battle of Salamis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns the whole run for 'Former king' round, giving XERXE. The whole clue also describes the king: Xerxes' fleet was beaten at Salamis in 480 BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes I of Persia was a past monarch whose navy was routed by the Greeks at Salamis.

clue.text: Many high-flyers get into this other type of crossword — and put a spurt on

parts.note: the Jumbo is The Times's extra-large crossword, another type besides the daily one
a jet is a spurt of liquid or gas

explanation.surface: Fans of a giant puzzle get stuck into it and hurry to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flyers' suggests achievers, but here it means air passengers, hundreds of whom fit in one large airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-bodied passenger aircraft carries hundreds of people, who board it to fly high.

clue.text: One trying to stop fighting of turbulent marrieds

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up and disordered, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peacemaker tries to calm a stormy married couple's rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One trying to stop fighting' looks like a marriage counsellor, but it is someone seeking to remove weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes away arms is working to end conflict, so a peacemaker of that kind.

clue.text: New missile contract

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A fresh weapons deal is signed.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to become smaller or tighter, which is to become less wide.

clue.text: Noise of engine, entering Victoria turned low

parts.note: VR, Victoria Regina, is the royal cypher of Queen Victoria

indicators.note: turned says the word for a cow's call is flipped round

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: A car revs as it comes into Victoria station and drops speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective about pitch, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Vroom imitates the roar of a motor being revved.

clue.text: One food store caught in check, in other words

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces go inside the word for check

parts.note: to vet something is to check it
I is the Roman numeral one
a deli, delicatessen, is a food shop
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A single grocer is caught during an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet, abbreviated viz., is Latin for namely, introducing a restatement or specification.

clue.text: Block that's part of prison? Not according to Lovelace

definitions.meaning: to obstruct or deliberately hold up, as in parliamentary delaying tactics

definitions.text: that's part of prison? Not according to Lovelace
definitions.meaning: Richard Lovelace wrote '... do not a prison make', so by his account masonry is no jail

explanation.surface: A cell block seems part of any jail, though a seventeenth-century poet disagreed.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct a process by delaying tactics, or a masonry barrier of the kind a poet said no jail was made of.

clue.text: Protest by workers about Jack's informal contact with public

indicators.note: about says the protest word goes around the sailor here

parts.note: a walkout is a strike where workers leave the job
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman

explanation.surface: Dock workers strike over a sailor's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack's' stands for 'Jack is': both Jack and AB mean a sailor. Here the answer is a royal or political figure meeting crowds informally.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is a stroll by a dignitary among the public to meet people informally.

clue.text: Produce order, say, to impose restrictions

indicators.note: say tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: to straighten up a room is to produce order in it

explanation.surface: A manager issues a command intended to rein people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce order' sounds like issuing a command, but it means tidying, the sense of straighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to restrict or confine, as in straitened circumstances.

clue.text: It's terrible to evict drunk, but that's an order

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel about and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Throwing out a drunk seems harsh, but the boss commanded it.
explanation.definitionFit: A directive is an official instruction, a command given by an authority.

clue.text: Man appearing ragged in torn piece of cloth

indicators.note: in says the scrambled word sits inside the word for torn

parts.note: rent, past tense of rend, means torn

indicators.note: ragged means tattered and disordered, so the letters of the word Man are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in rags turns up wearing torn clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man appearing ragged' looks like a description of a tramp; 'ragged' is the anagram signal, and 'torn' is a past participle standing for a word that means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A remnant is a leftover scrap at the end of a bolt of fabric.

clue.text: Modest grade got by girl in form

parts.note: C is a middling, unremarkable mark in school grading
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl in school gets an unspectacular mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is the British word for a school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a form is a group of pupils taught together, also called a year group.

clue.text: Composer of some crosswords met an aficionado

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzle fan meets the setter of some of their favourite crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer, writer of The Bartered Bride and Má vlast.

clue.text: New shoot appears about then

parts.note: the season when fresh growth sprouts from plants, read as a time of year rather than an event

explanation.definitionFit: Spring is the season between winter and summer, when plants put out fresh growth.

clue.text: Writer departs with a letter for Corinthians

parts.note: Charles Lamb was an English essayist, author of the Essays of Elia
D stands for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: An author leaves with a message for the Corinthians, as St Paul did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter for Corinthians' points to St Paul's epistles, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet, as used in Corinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh character of the Greek alphabet, which the people of Corinth wrote in.

clue.text: Is this clock incapable of striking one?

definitions.text: Is this clock incapable of striking one?

parts.words: Is this clock incapable of striking one?
parts.note: a chiming clock that strikes the hour again on demand never strikes just once, as it keeps going over the hours

explanation.definitionFit: A clock or watch that strikes the last hour again when a button is pressed, so it repeats rather than striking a single time.

clue.text: Fare from India -fellow returned it with thanks

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: returned says the run of two short words is written backwards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A man hands back an Indian dish with a word of gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns IT and TA together, giving ATTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapatti is an unleavened flatbread, a staple food of the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Indication of constant pressure is nothing to lawyers

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
the Bar is the collective body of barristers

explanation.surface: Legal folk shrug off a stress warning as meaning nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constant pressure' suggests stress at work, but it is atmospheric pressure on a weather map.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart, a line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: A tint I developed for red hair

indicators.note: developed, as film is developed, says the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A hairdresser applies a dye that turns hair red.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is the bright auburn colour of hair seen in the Venetian painter's portraits.

clue.text: Mean American smashed advertisement about Western

parts.note: smashed and tight both mean drunk

explanation.surface: A stingy Yank, drunk, gripes about a cowboy-film commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightwad is US slang for a miser, a stingy person.
